For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Heard Mr. Krunal Verma, learned counsel appearing
for the petitioner.
2. The  petitioner  sought  quashing  of  the  First
Information Report in connection with Crime No. 305 of
2019  registered  with  Police  Station  Sadar,  District
Nagpur City, Nagpur registered under Section 66(B) of the
1

## Page 461

Information Technology Act, 2000 and under Section 3(1)
(c) of the Official Secrets Act, 1923.  Subsequently,
charge-sheet came to be filed under Charge-sheet No.246
of 2020 before the Court of the Judicial Magistrate,
First Class, Court No.6, Nagpur, Maharashtra.  
3. Learned counsel contends that the High Court having
clearly  found  that  Section  3(1)(c)  of  the  Official
Secrets Act was not attracted, absolved the petitioner
from the ingredients of that offence. However, dealing
with the Information Technology Act, the High Court found
that while the allegations in the FIR would not attract
Section 66 (B), it attracts Section 66, since Section
43(b)  appeared  to  have  been  prima  facie violated.
Learned counsel submits that in the petitioner’s own
petition these findings have been recorded.
4. We clarify that while there is no ground to quash
the First Information Report, any observation made by the
High Court about Section 43 (b) and Section 66 being
attracted are not conclusive.  The Trial Court, while
framing charges, shall independently apply its mind based
on the material furnished to it and frame such charge as
is attracted or if none of the charges are attracted,
discharge the petitioner.  The High Court’s observations
need to be understood only for the purpose of dealing
with the petition to quash the First Information Report.
2

## Page 462

5. With  the  above  observations,  the  Special  Leave
Petition is disposed of.

1. Delay condoned.
2. The petitioner who had been denied bail by the High Court,
has been in judicial custody for more         than 3 years and 6
months, in connection with FIR No. 54 of 2023 registered at PS
Kotwali Nagar, District Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh for the offence
punishable under 307 of the Indian Penal Code (for short “the
IPC”).
3. The petitioner is accused of attacking the complainant with
sticks, along with some associates, with the intention to kill
the  complainant.  It  is  alleged  that  in  the  attack  the
complainant sustained serious injuries and that the petitioner
had been released from jail only two days prior to the alleged
incident.
4. The Chargesheet had been filed on 20.09.2023, and the
charges were framed on 14.12.2023. However, as submitted by the
Learned Counsel for the Respondent-State of Uttar Pradesh, only
1 witness has been examined thus far, out of 6 witnesses as per
Diary No.38902/2026                                               2 

## Page 474

the chargesheet.
5. The attack is said to have been made on a jail warden, and
the allegation is that the petitioner was released two days
before the incident; the motive being a prior quarrel during
imprisonment. Though Section 307 of the IPC has been charged,
the injury sustained is a small, shallow bleeding cut on the top
left of the head.
6. On a prima facie consideration of the material on record,
we are of the opinion that the petitioner can be released on
bail, subject to such terms and conditions that the District and
Sessions  Judge/F.T.C.  Second,  Sultanpur  (the  jurisdictional
court)  may  deem  fit  to  impose.  Ordered  accordingly.  The
petitioner shall cooperate with the trial.
7. With the above directions, the Special Leave Petition is
disposed of.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed
of.

Court in connection with FIR No. 5137002250074 of 2025 filed
at  PS  Amba,  District  Aurangabad,  Bihar  for  the  offence
punishable under Sections 80 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya
Sanhita (for short “the BNS”) and Sections 3 and 4 of the
Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961. 
2. The prosecution case arises out of the death of the daughter
of the complainant within one year of marriage to the son of
the petitioner. The cause of death was found to be consumption
of poison. The petitioner, being the mother-in-law of the
deceased, along with the co-accused father-in-law and husband,
is alleged to have assaulted and demanded dowry, as well as
having threatened to kill her.
3. Notice was issued in this matter on 29.07.2026, along with the
direction that no coercive steps shall be taken against the
petitioner,  subject  to  her  full  cooperation  with  the
investigation. 
4. Regular bail has been granted to the son by the High Court on
16.03.2026. 
5. The order impugned herein was challenged by the learned
Counsel for the petitioner on various grounds, such as there
being  only  general  and  omnibus  allegations  against  the
petitioner, and that the petitioner was an elderly woman with
clean antecedents. 
SLP(Crl.)  No.13773/2026 2

6. We order that in the event of arrest of the petitioner in
connection with the offence enumerated above, she shall be
released on bail, subject to such terms and conditions that
the Investigating Officer (for short “I.O.”) may deem fit
impose, on condition also of continued cooperation in the
investigation. 
7. Once the petitioner is released on bail by the I.O., on
directions issued by the I.O. or summons issued by the
Additional  Sessions  Judge,  Aurangabad  (the  jurisdictional
court), the petitioner shall appear before the jurisdictional
court and furnish bail bonds and ensure due appearance in the
trial.

We have heard the petitioner, who has appeared in person.
In this writ petition filed under Article 32 of the  
Constitution of India, the following prayers are sought-
“a) issue a writ in the nature of mandamus,
order, direction or any other appropriate writ
seeking to immediately Stay the proceedings of
the quashing  cases vide nos-APL-1485/2025, APL-
521/2022, APL-952/2026, pending at High Court of
Bombay,  Bench  at  Nagpur,  and  also  stay  the
interim order dated 29/04/2026, passed in APL-
521/2022 and APL-1485/2025, along  with,
a) issue a writ in the nature of mandamus, order,
direction or any other appropriate writ seeking
to restrain the respondents no- 6, 7 & 8 (accused
persons in FIR-468/2021) from travelling abroad
or leaving the country till the final judgement
of the Sessions Trial-196/2022, pending in the
1

## Page 506

Court of District Judge-15, Additional Sessions
Judge, Nagpur District  Court,
b) issue a writ in the .nature of mandamus,
order, direction or any other appropriate writ
thereby  giving the  direction to  tlie accused
persons in FIR-468/2021, i.e respondents 6,7 & 8
to submit their passports in the Trial Court in
Sessions Trial-196/2022,
c) issue a writ in the nature of mandamus, order,
direction or any other appropriate writ seeking
the Sessions Trial-196/2022, under the eye and
supervision of this Hon'ble Court,
d) Pass any other or such orders as this court
may  deem  fit  and  proper  in  the  interest  of
justice.”
On  perusal of the prayers, we note that the proceedings 
for quashing of the cases filed by the accused are pending
before  the  Nagpur  Bench  of  the  Bombay  High  Court.  The
petitioner is a party in those proceedings. The grievance of
the petitioner is with regard to prayers (a) and (b) reliefs.
We reserve liberty to the petitioner herein to file an
application or a separate petition before the Bombay High
Court  or  alternatively,  before  the  Sessions  Court  where
Sessions Trial No.196/2022 is pending to seek the reliefs at
prayers (a) and (b) above.
If the applications seeking prayers (a) and (b) above,
have been filed by the petitioner herein, the same shall also
be considered expeditiously. 
The petitioner is also at liberty to seek any other
relief with regard to accused, who have been  tried in Session
Trial No.196/2022 either before the Sessions Court or before
the High Court in accordance with law.

Special Leave Petition, especially due to the reason that it may

unnecessarily delaying the ongoing arbitration proceedings.
3. Consequently, the Special Leave Petition is dismissed.  The
parties may approach the learned Arbitrator for continuation of the
arbitration proceedings. However, the question of law is kept open
to be gone into in the appropriate proceedings.

SLP(C) No. 9417/2020
5. During the course of hearing, learned counsel for the parties
have been persuaded to agree that the learned sole Arbitrator
appointed by the High Court shall be the Presiding Arbitrator and
both parties shall nominate their respective Arbitrators. 
6. The needful shall be done within two weeks. The three-member
Arbitral Tribunal shall thereafter proceed with the matter in
accordance with law.  
7. It goes without saying that the learned Arbitral Tribunal
shall proceed/continue from the stage it had already reached. 
8. The Special Leave Petition is, accordingly, disposed of. It is
clarified that we have not expressed any opinion on merits of the
case/proceedings.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand closed.

THE STATE OF JHARKHAND & ANR.                      Respondent(s)
(FOR ADMISSION)
 
Date : 06-08-2026 This petition was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K.V. VISWANATHAN
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ARUN PALLI
For Petitioner(s) : 
                    Mr. Rajan Rai,Adv.
                    Ms. Mohini Priya, AOR
                   
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Heard Mr.Rajan Rai, learned counsel appearing for
the petitioner.
2. Learned counsel submits that the impugned order of
the High Court has not directed 20% or more of the fine
amount or compensation amount to be deposited as required
under Section 148(1) of the Negotiable  Instruments Act,
1881 (for short, “the NI Act”).  Learned counsel also
submits that this Court in the case of  Surinder Singh
1

## Page 724

Deswal alias Colonel S.S.Deswal & Ors. v. Virender Gandhi1
has held that the word “may” in Section 148 of the NI Act
is to  be construed as “shall” and if the Court deems it
fit  not  to  direct  any  deposit,  it  can  only  be  in
exceptional cases, where special reasons are required to
be assigned.  It has been further held that the direction
to deposit under Section 148 of the NI Act is applicable
even on an application filed by the accused under Section
389  of  the  Code  of  Criminal  Procedure,  1973  for
suspension of sentence.
3. We grant liberty to the petitioner to bring this
fact to the knowledge of the High Court by moving an
appropriate application.  In case of any adverse order,
the petitioner will be at liberty to file a Special Leave
Petition not only against the said adverse order but also
against the impugned order.
4. With  the  above  observations,  the  Special  Leave
Petition is disposed of.
5. Pending  application,  if  any,  shall  also  stand
disposed of.
(ANITA MALHOTRA)                          (MANOJ KUMAR)
  DEPUTY REGISTRAR                          COURT MASTER

For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. We are not inclined to interfere with the impugned judgment and order of
the High Court; hence, the special leave petition is dismissed.
3. However, we need to make a parting observation.
1

## Page 794

4. A Single Judge of the High Court while disposing of the application for
modification filed by the petitioner, i.e., I.A. No.1 of 2026 as withdrawn and
reserving the petitioner’s liberty to file a writ appeal has observed that the
petitioner is granted the benefit of limitation under Section 14 of the Limitation
Act, 1963.
5. We are surprised that the Single Judge made such an observation. It is not
for a Single Judge to dictate terms for filing of an appeal before a Division
Bench. Whether or not a party would be entitled to the benefit of Section 14
should have been left entirely for the intra-appellate court to examine, if at all
any appeal were carried before it. Observation of this nature is bound to create
chaos and confusion. 
6. We treat this as an aberration and hope and trust that there will be no
recurrence of such an error.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
  (RASHMI DHYANI PANT)                       (SUDHIR KUMAR SHARMA)

Maharashtra  and  Ors.1 and  Shalini  Vs.  New  English  High  School
Association and Ors.2 together with the Full Bench decision of the High Court
in Arun Sonowane Vs. State of Maharashtra 3, the Division Bench directed
that the respondent be reinstated in service and given continuity of service for

invalidated by the Scrutiny Committee. However, the High Court having set
aside such decision, the same are under challenge before this Court in SLP(C)

before a coordinate Bench on 14th August, 2026.

hearing of this appeal.

coordinate Bench.

therein, who was denied bail, though was the son of the couple
who were granted bail, was not the son who was alleged with
the crime of abduction.

Arman – the petitioner herein – is the brother of the said
person. Finding parity with the father and mother who were
granted anticipatory bail, we find that the applicant herein
shall also be released on similar terms.

cooperate  with  the  investigation,  and  appear  before  the
jurisdictional court as and when directed.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioner before us has been sentenced to life
imprisonment, and is stated to have been incarcerated for 18 years.
2. After dismissal of his Criminal Appeal up to this Court,
he has now applied for premature release on 21.10.2025. 
3. It is stated that no decision has been taken on that
application, by the Competent Authority, prompting the petitioner
to approach this Court by way of the instant Writ Petition under
Article 32 of the Constitution of India.
4. We have heard learned counsel for the petitioner and
carefully perused the material placed on record.
5. At the outset, we may observe that the petitioner ought
to have approached the jurisdictional High Court for the desired
relief. 

## Page 962

2
6. However, having regard to the nature of the prayer(s)
made, we dispose of the instant Writ Petition without expressing
any opinion on the same, and with a direction to the State of Uttar
Pradesh and the Director General (Prisons) and/or other Authorities
to consider the petitioner’s pending application seeking premature
release in accordance with the relevant Government Policy and take
an appropriate decision within a period of three months.
7. As a result, the pending interlocutory application also
stands disposed of.
